context: Riku-teen helps Sho-young assemble a model airplane.
purpose: Older teen patiently helping younger child craft.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 陸くん、組み立て、難しい!
lines.en: Riku, this is so hard to put together!
lines.style: Frustrated but not despairing. Small voice, slightly strained. Reaches toward Riku with the piece, asking for help not demanding it. Genuine strain without drama.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.en: Take your time with it — just place your fingers here.
lines.style: Calm, unhurried. Leans in slightly to show him. Warm instruction, the tone of someone who has done this before and isn't worried. Almost gentle.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 丁度、この位置で合うかな?
lines.en: Does it fit right here, do you think?
lines.style: Tentative, checking his own work. Soft questioning lilt. Genuinely uncertain but engaged. The careful concentration of a kid learning something.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: うん、足元、しっかり持って。
lines.en: Yeah, just hold the bottom part steady for me.
lines.style: Encouraging without condescension. Light, easy tone. The older person who actually trusts the younger one to do their part. Warm presence.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 完成したら、飛行できる?
lines.en: Once we finish it, will it actually fly?
lines.style: Hope creeping into wonder. Eager but not loud. The kind of question a kid asks when they're starting to believe something magical might be real.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: ええ模型や、ちゃんと飛ぶで!
lines.en: Yeah, a model like this will fly really well.
lines.style: Quiet pride in his voice. Reassurance that feels earned. Slight warmth on the affirmation. The confidence of someone showing a kid something that works.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: やった、頑張ってよかった!
lines.en: Yes! I'm so glad we kept trying!
lines.style: Bright, genuine joy. Not performed excitement, but real relief and delight. Bounces slightly in the voice. The pure happiness of something working.
